rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis adds ~5 at.% Ti, while the paper adds 20 at.% Re; both are compositional modifications of NbMoTaW, but the specific element and amount differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation testing, but the paper only performed room-temperature He-ion irradiation and nanoindentation/compression; no high-temperature testing was done.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes grain-boundary segregation of Ti to enhance cohesion and ductility, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth and embrittlement.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved room-temperature ductility without loss of high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance; the paper reports improved He-irradiation resistance (less hardening, less embrittlement) but does not address room-temperature ductility or high-temperature performance.
